text:
incident-bot: ALERT: increased tail latency observed in prod-west-1 (p95=360ms, p99=2.3s). streaming stalls up 3x. alert=INC-2026-0316-02

arjun: getting paging on this. I see a bunch of recent escalations from support between 13:10-13:15 UTC. grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/serving/west-1/latency

lina: quick look 13:12 UTC - KV slab_eviction_rate jumped; prefill queue > decoder queue by ~4x. this smells like prefill saturation and uneven slab allocation -> fragmentation.

frank: confirming. hot-path model is model-x-large. warm pool is low on warm workers, fallback cold starts rising.

arjun: steps? options: 1) soft throttle low-priority traffic 2) shift a subset of traffic to warm pool (warmup) 3) bump slab target util temporarily 4) reduce prefill concurrency to match decoder 5) emergency rolling restart to defrag slabs.

devops-jane: I can push an ingress throttle for free-tier/orgs < 10k tokens/day. should cut burstiness quickly. want me to pull the trigger?

support-jen: yes please, do it. customers flagged: delta-inc, gamma-beta. letting them know.

frank: while that happens I'll prepare a warm-pool shift. we have a warm pool in eu-west but can spin up more warm workers in west-1 if infra lends capacity.

arjun: go ahead with ingress throttle + warm-pool shift. also reduce prefill_workers on model-x-large to 6 from 20 and increase decoder_workers to 24 to rebalance.

ops-bot: action requested: ingress-throttle apply by devops-jane 3210004450

devops-jane: applying ingress throttle now. command: 
```
PATCH /api/edge/config
{"rate_limit":{"selector":"non-enterprise","value":"80r/s"}}
```

ops-bot: ingress-throttle applied by devops-jane - rollout started 3210004453

lina: watch: after throttle, burst traffic dropped ~40%. KV eviction_rate decreased by ~45% across pool. cache_hit_ratio improved 0.76 -> 0.9.

frank: warming additional workers into warm-pool: 
```
kubectl scale deployment/warm-worker -n prod --replicas=12 --selector=zone=west-1
```

frank: spun up 8 extra warm workers, warm handshake completed for most hot models. cold-start fallback rate halved.

arjun: applying worker config change for model-x-large: 
```
POST /admin/pools/reconfigure
{"pool":"west-1-x-large","prefill_workers":6,"decoder_workers":24}
```

arjun: change applied 13:17:12 UTC.

lina: after adjustments p95=190ms, p99=520ms, streaming stalls dropping. still seeing discrete tail spikes correlated with slab GC cycles (~every 7-10m).

arjun: to reduce fragmentation, I'm going to toggle KV_SLAB_PADDING=1 to add headroom (temp). will roll env change one AZ at a time.

devops-jane: ready to set env var and restart gradually. command: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/serving-worker KV_SLAB_PADDING=1 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-worker -n prod --selector=zone=west-1
```

ops-bot: slab-padding env set and rolling restart started by devops-jane 3210004700

lina: after first AZ restart eviction spikes muted, fragmentation metric improved. p99 down to 280ms.

support-jen: delta-inc support notes: sessions recovered within ~10m of mitigation, they reported intermittent stalls but are back to normal.

arjun: proposed follow-ups: - add decoder backpressure signal to prefill controller - adaptive prefill cap based on recent eviction rate - slab fragmentation alert (sustained fragmentation>threshold) - capacity plan for larger warm pool for high-memory models. Creating INF ticket INF-2026-1456.

frank: agree. also want to run a sim test with synthetic burst traffic to validate adaptive prefill throttling.

olivia: taking handoff for night. key watch metrics: slab_eviction_rate, cache_hit_ratio, streaming_stall_rate, fallback_cold_start_rate. I ack.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied (ingress throttle, prefill->decoder rebalance, warm-pool scale, slab padding + rolling restarts). severity: SEV3 -> monitoring. incident_id=INC-2026-0316-02

arjun: adding final note: estimated customer impact window ~13m (13:10-13:23 UTC). postmortem owners assigned: lina + frank.

lina: will attach dashboard links and logs to incident doc.

arjun: thanks all. follow-up meeting scheduled tomorrow to discuss longer-term fixes.
